transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place. I, um, well, I guess the main reason I'm here is that I've been struggling a little bit at work lately. I manage a few health clinics, and normally I'm pretty good at keeping things running smoothly, you know? But recently, anything that takes real sitting-down brain work... like those monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

I don't mean to sound lazy, I really don't. It's just that I find myself putting those things off, even when I know they're important. I'm sure everyone procrastinates a little, right? But it's been getting a bit harder to push through it lately. Is that... is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Have you experienced this kind of difficulty focusing and getting started on tasks since you were younger, like in school, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's probably been around for a while. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything! I was actually pretty bright, or at least that's what my teachers always told my parents. 

But, you know, they did always add that I was... well, maybe a bit of a daydreamer? I'd kind of get lost in my own thoughts sometimes. And I guess I was a little disorganized back in elementary school. I'd misplace worksheets here and there, or forget to actually hand in the homework I'd finished. It wasn't because I didn't care! It's just... well, my mom actually had to get into the habit of checking my backpack every single night just to make sure things got turned in. 

I think a lot of kids go through a phase like that, though, don't they? It's pretty normal for a little boy to be a bit scatterbrained, right?
Aside from the trouble focusing, have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down, less interested in things you used to enjoy, or unusually tired?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I feel pretty good overall, mood-wise! I'm not, you know, depressed or anything. I still really enjoy my weekends, spending time with my family, and I have plenty of energy for the things I like doing. 

I don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself or just too tired to work. It's really just that mental block with the paperwork and the big planning tasks. Everything else is... well, it's fine. I'm generally a pretty positive person, I think. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here.

Does this trouble concentrating and getting started happen across many different kinds of tasks and situations—at work, home, or in conversations—or is it pretty much limited to those specific paperwork and planning tasks you mentioned?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, it's mostly just the work stuff. The reports, the spreadsheets... things like that. 

I mean, I suppose my wife might say I can be a little forgetful at home sometimes? Like, maybe I'll start organizing the garage and then get sidetracked fixing a squeaky door hinge instead. But I always get back to it eventually! I really try to be helpful around the house, I promise. I'm not just ignoring my chores or anything. 

And in conversations... I think I'm a pretty good listener! Sometimes my mind might wander just a tiny bit if someone's telling a really long story, but I'm sure everyone does that, right? I always make sure to nod and smile so they know I'm paying attention. I wouldn't want to be rude. So, yeah, I'd say it's really just those big work projects where it's a noticeable issue. Is that... does that sound like what you usually hear from people?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Oh, no... no, I don't think so. I mean, I sit through long meetings all the time at work—I manage a health clinic, so I have to be pretty professional and composed, you know? I definitely don't have trouble sitting still or anything like that. 

I mean, sure, maybe I'll tap my pen or bounce my leg a little under the desk if a meeting goes on for a really long time, but... I think that's just normal, right? Everyone gets a little stiff when they've been sitting in one chair for two hours. 

And as for interrupting... oh, I'd absolutely hate to do that. I really try to be respectful and wait my turn to speak. I wouldn't ever want to make anyone feel like I wasn't valuing what they had to say. And I'm usually pretty careful about decisions, especially when it affects my staff. I definitely don't just jump into things without thinking them through. 

So, no, I don't think I'm impulsive or fidgety at all. That's... that's a good thing, right? Hopefully that means whatever is going on with my focus isn't too severe?
Do you often lose or misplace things you need for daily tasks, like keys, phone, or important documents, and has that been a lifelong pattern for you?

Oh, um... lose things? No, not really. I mean, I think I'm pretty organized overall. 

Sure, I guess every now and then I might have to look around for my car keys for a minute before I leave the house, but... well, that happens to everybody, doesn't it? I just try to keep everything in its place. I have a little bowl by the door for my keys and wallet, and I'm usually really good about using it. I wouldn't want to hold up my family or be late for work because I couldn't find my things. 

And important documents... no, I definitely don't lose those. With my job, I have to keep track of a lot of files, and I'm very careful not to misplace anything important. I'd be so embarrassed if I lost something a patient or one of my staff members needed. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I have a pattern of losing things at all. I try really hard to stay on top of all that. Does that... does that help rule out anything serious? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When you're trying to work on those reports or planning tasks, do you notice your attention frequently drifting away because of unrelated thoughts or things going on around you, making it hard to stay on track?

Well, um... I guess my mind does wander a little bit sometimes. But it's really not too bad! I mean, when I'm in a meeting, say, listening to a budget update... I really do try my best to pay attention. I know how important it is. 

But, you know, if someone's phone vibrates on the table, or if I hear people talking out in the hallway... sometimes my attention just sort of slips over to that for a second. Or even just a random thought pops into my head, like something I forgot to do for my bowling league, and before I know it, I realize I haven't heard the last few minutes of the presentation. 

I always feel terrible when it happens, and I really try to catch myself and tune back in quickly so nobody notices. I don't want anyone to think I don't care about their presentation. I just... I get a little sidetracked by things going on around me, I suppose. But I'm sure everyone gets distracted by hallway noise sometimes, right? It's perfectly normal to have your mind drift a little, isn't it?

Has this difficulty finishing reports and planning tasks ever caused real problems at work, like missing a deadline, receiving negative feedback from your supervisor, or having a project fall through?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's caused *real* problems, exactly. I mean, I'm definitely still getting by at work, and I still manage the clinic just fine! 

I guess... well, there have been a couple of times where a deadline might have slipped just a tiny bit. Nothing major, just... you know, I didn't quite finish a report on time, and my assistant had to kind of step in and help me pull the data together at the last minute so we could submit it. I felt awful about it, of course. I really hate making other people cover my gaps. 

And, um, I suppose I've had to send a few slightly embarrassing emails apologizing to my supervisor for being a day late on the scheduling plans. Or, you know, apologizing to the guys in my bowling league because I forgot to book the lanes until the very last second. 

But I always make sure it gets done eventually! And I always apologize profusely so people know I'm not doing it on purpose. It's not like I've ever had a whole project completely fall through or anything terrible like that. I'm still doing okay overall, right? I mean, everyone needs a little help from their coworkers sometimes, don't they?

Thinking back to elementary or middle school, did your teachers or parents ever mention that your daydreaming or disorganization was affecting your grades or getting you into trouble, like missing assignments or being reprimanded for careless mistakes?

Oh, wow, going back that far... um... well, I was definitely a good kid! My teachers always told my parents I was bright, which was really nice to hear. I certainly wasn't a troublemaker or anything like that. 

I guess... well, they did mention to my parents that I was always daydreaming a bit. Just, you know, having a good imagination and getting a little lost in my own thoughts sometimes. And... well, I suppose I did have a bit of a habit of losing worksheets or forgetting to actually turn in my homework after I did it. 

It sounds so silly now, but my mother actually had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure I had everything and would hand it in the next day. I always felt a little guilty that she had to spend her time doing that for me, but she just wanted to help me stay organized. 

But, I mean, a lot of little boys are like that, aren't they? It's pretty normal for kids in elementary school to have their heads in the clouds and need their mom to check their folders, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student. I always tried my best to be good for my teachers.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I wouldn't say it's caused *real* problems, exactly. I mean, I'm definitely still getting by at work, and I still manage the clinic just fine! 

I guess... well, there have been a couple of times where a deadline might have slipped just a tiny bit. Nothing major, just... you know, I didn't quite finish a report on time, and my assistant had to kind of step in and help me pull the data together at the last minute so we could submit it. I felt awful about it, of course. I really hate making other people cover my gaps. 

And, um, I suppose I've had to send a few slightly embarrassing emails apologizing to my supervisor for being a day late on the scheduling plans. Or, you know, apologizing to the guys in my bowling league because I forgot to book the lanes until the very last second. 

But I always make sure it gets done eventually! And I always apologize profusely so people know I'm not doing it on purpose. It's not like I've ever had a whole project completely fall through or anything terrible like that. I'm still doing okay overall, right? I mean, everyone needs a little help from their coworkers sometimes, don't they?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the attentional difficulties caused noticeable functional impairment in childhood (e.g., grades, teacher reports, need for reminders) across more than one setting, to confirm childhood-onset impairment required for ADHD diagnosis.
doctor.question: Thinking back to elementary or middle school, did your teachers or parents ever mention that your daydreaming or disorganization was affecting your grades or getting you into trouble, like missing assignments or being reprimanded for careless mistakes?

patient.answer:
Oh, wow, going back that far... um... well, I was definitely a good kid! My teachers always told my parents I was bright, which was really nice to hear. I certainly wasn't a troublemaker or anything like that. 

I guess... well, they did mention to my parents that I was always daydreaming a bit. Just, you know, having a good imagination and getting a little lost in my own thoughts sometimes. And... well, I suppose I did have a bit of a habit of losing worksheets or forgetting to actually turn in my homework after I did it. 

It sounds so silly now, but my mother actually had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure I had everything and would hand it in the next day. I always felt a little guilty that she had to spend her time doing that for me, but she just wanted to help me stay organized. 

But, I mean, a lot of little boys are like that, aren't they? It's pretty normal for kids in elementary school to have their heads in the clouds and need their mom to check their folders, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student. I always tried my best to be good for my teachers.
